transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-02-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood CSM), Priya (Edenbridge Head of Security), Graham (Platform), Maya (Product), Alex (Infra)

Summary: quick weekly sync to hand off SSO configuration, confirm audit log schema, and tune data retention rules for POC. Ran through a few recent incidents in the test environment and next steps for artifacts and a short bench run.

Topics: SSO metadata / IdP certs, audit log format and delivery (syslog vs API), data retention policies and export, SOC2 artefacts, short latency bench for peak hour simulation.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone, thanks for joining, mic checks, can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Priya: yes, loud and clear. sorry running slightly late earlier.
[00:08] Liam: good morning from my side, quick agenda — SSO, audit logs, retention, then open items from last week.
[00:15] Graham: sounds good. we also had that failed replay where the logs were missing some fields, we'll show that.
[00:20] Sofia: perfect — quick note, i'll drop the SOC2 report link in chat after the call; it's redacted for PII but has the controls matrix.
[00:28] Priya: appreciate that. one ask up front: we need to see evidence of encryption-at-rest + KMS integration. last time the doc had KMS spelled out as K-M-S and the example was a bit generic.
[00:36] Sofia: yes so the private deployment we are testing uses customer KMS via envelope encryption, we'll include the KMS key id, and a diagram of key access.
[00:44] Alex: can you confirm whether logs written to the audit bucket are encrypted with the same key or a different key? that's part of our compliance checklist.
[00:51] Liam: good question — currently logs are written to a separate audit bucket and by default we use the same KMS alias but we can scope separate keys per project if you want. it's a config flag on the retention policy.
[01:02] Maya: minor thing — for retention, our legal team wants 7yrs for some PHI-adjacent telemetry, while other traces can be 90 days. can Redwood support per-stream retention?
[01:10] Liam: yes, retention per stream is supported, we map ingest tags to retention rules. the gotcha is that indexing and KV cache artifacts (the model side cache) can have different retention semantics, so we'll need to map those.
[01:20] Priya: about SSO — we tried the test assertion earlier and saw a 401; the error showed unknown audience. we think the ACS URL mismatch might be the cause.
[01:28] Alex: i have the metadata from Okta here, i'll send it, but can you confirm the exact ACS your SP expects?
[01:34] Sofia: sure, the ACS we provide for the private control plane is https://controlplane.redwood.local/saml/acs — note that's the test host, for prod it'll be your VPC host. i'll include the metadata.
[01:44] [00:44] Priya: ok, also need to confirm nameid format for user email vs persistent id.
[01:48] Liam: we accept both, but user.email is recommended for mapping to users; persistent id works if you prefer. we've seen mismatch when customer maps to an internal id.
[02:00] Graham: on the log schema: we replayed the traffic from last Wednesday and several entries were missing the request_id field, which breaks our correlation. is that a Redwood schema change?
[02:10] Liam: hmm — that's likely from a truncation issue in continuous batching at token boundary. the runtime should emit request_id as part of the header object; sometimes ASR of the agent drops it. we'll run a targeted replay.
[02:22] Sofia: can you capture the example log lines and paste them in the shared spreadsheet? that will help us map fields.
[02:27] Graham: yes i'll put them in. we also noticed the timestamp timezone was UTC in some entries and local in others — makes alignment messy.
[02:34] Liam: noted, our timestamps should always be RFC3339 UTC; if you see local offsets that's probably from your syslog forwarder adding local timezone. we'll add a validation check on ingest.
[02:45] Priya: SOC2 — will you provide the control matrix and the recent Type II report? we need to show that to our audit team next week.
[02:52] Sofia: yes, i'll upload the Type II redacted PDF, controls matrix, and our pen test summary. link will be in the follow-up email.
[03:00] Priya: great. can you also confirm if Redwood can do per-tenant log separation for the POC? we prefer isolated buckets.
[03:08] Liam: yes, isolation per tenant/bucket is supported; there is a tiny overhead for lifecycle rules but it's straightforward.
[03:15] Maya: question on export: can we stream audit logs to our SIEM, or is it batch only?
[03:19] Liam: both — streaming over syslog/HTTPS is supported; we also provide batched S3 deliveries every hour. the streaming uses mutual TLS to your collector.
[03:28] Alex: for mutual TLS, do we use client certs from our side or Redwood CA? what rotates certs?
[03:33] Sofia: you can provide client certs — ideal for enterprise. cert rotation can be automated via your cert manager or we can accept rotated certs via API. we'll send the cert rotation playbook.
[03:45] [05:00] (short silence while team checks notes)
[05:12] Priya: quick tangent — we saw two auth failures yesterday during the bench runs, thought it might be a clock skew. Okta logs show an invalid signature on the assertion.
[05:20] Alex: right, I noticed our IdP clock was 30s skewed; fixed that. will re-run and retest.
[05:27] Sofia: good catch. If that persists, we'll also check the signing algorithm mismatch; some older IdPs sign with sha1-resig or legacy algs.
[05:36] Liam: one more thing — the runtime has an optional assertion caching layer to reduce IdP requests; it's off by default in POC. if you want it on, it reduces round trips but introduces token TTL complexity.
[05:50] Graham: we might want it on for prod, but POC keep it off.
[05:55] Sofia: noted.
[06:00] (screen share notes)
[06:04] Liam: i'm going to walk through the small replay log we captured — i've pasted a snippet: "{timestamp: 2027-02-18T14:03:12Z, request_id: -, user: maya@edenbridge, action: generate, model: rw-7b-q8, latency_ms: 1800}" — you can see request_id is a hyphen, that's the issue.
[06:18] Priya: that makes correlation impossible; we rely on it for incident investigation.
[06:22] Liam: agreed — our replay shows this happens when the front proxy truncates at 8k tokens and request header falls off. fix is to adjust Nginx buffer settings or enable prefix caching at the runtime so header is preserved.
[06:34] Alex: we can adjust buffer; does Redwood have recommended proxy settings?
[06:38] Liam: yes, i'll send the nginx.conf snippets and a short check list.
[06:44] Sofia: also adding to next steps: implement nginx fix in staging and rerun replay.
[06:50] [12:00] (discussion about retention specifics)
[12:05] Maya: legal provided the retention matrix — some log types flagged as PD or PHI should be exported monthly for long-term archive. does Redwood support tiered export?
[12:12] Liam: yes, we can tier to cold storage after 90 days and keep metadata hot. exports can be scheduled or policy-triggered.
[12:20] Priya: what about data subject requests? if a user asks for deletion do we have a purge API that ties to the retention schedule?
[12:28] Liam: there is a purge API and a retention webhook that can trigger policy changes. note that for immutable audit logs we recommend redaction rather than deletion in some jurisdictions; we'll need to document the legal constraints per dataset.
[12:40] Sofia: we also support export of audit trails for e-discovery — we can produce a signed package with checksums.
[12:46] Graham: good. for compliance we'll need the checksum manifest in the artifact.
[12:50] Sofia: done, we'll include that.
[13:00] (brief cross-talk about scheduling a latency bench)
[13:05] Noah: quick ask — can we run a short 1-hour peak bench next Thursday to reproduce the latency spike? want to invite Edenbridge infra to observe.
[13:12] Alex: yes, Thurs works. what do you need from us?
[13:15] Noah: ideally service account with write-only access to run synthetic traffic, and a window with peak config. Liam will provide the bench script.
[13:22] Liam: i'll send the script and also a dockerized runner you can run from your VPC to avoid cross-region noise.
[13:30] [25:00] (deeper debug on audit ingestion delays)
[25:10] Graham: ingestion delay — some logs arrived with 4-5 minute delay, that could break SLA. is that expected?
[25:18] Liam: default is within 1 minute under normal load; the 4-5 minute happened when we hit a backlog in continuous batching due to model stall. there's a small buffer we can increase to reduce backpressure.
[25:30] Priya: what's the impact to ordering guarantees? we need to ensure chronological ordering for the investigation pipeline.
[25:37] Liam: we maintain causal ordering per request_id, but if request_id missing ordering can be off. increasing buffer keeps order but increases memory footprint. we'll propose parameters based on your peak QPS.
[25:50] Sofia: we'll run the bench and capture latency + ingestion metrics, then propose a buffer size.
[25:58] Priya: please also include the ingestion SLA language for the POC contract extension.
[26:05] Sofia: noted.
[26:10] (15 minute mark)
[26:12] Priya: on SSO user mapping — will Redwood mirror group roles into RBAC? we want groups from Okta mapped to internal roles for audit purposes.
[26:20] Liam: yes, we map SAML attributes to roles; we support group sync and SCIM for full provisioning if you need it.
[26:28] Maya: SCIM would be ideal for provisioning service accounts.
[26:31] Liam: we can enable SCIM in the dedicated control plane. it's behind a feature flag for the POC.
[26:37] Alex: will SCIM require outbound access to Okta? we lock egress heavily.
[26:41] Liam: SCIM calls are initiated from our control plane; for private deployments we can proxy SCIM over your network or run the SCIM agent inside your VPC.
[26:50] Priya: good. make that optional and documented.
[26:55] [35:00] (wrap up and recap)
[35:05] Sofia: OK recap — Sofia will share SOC2 artifacts and pen test summary by Thursday; Alex will supply SAML metadata and certs; Liam will run audit-log replay, share nginx config and bench script; Noah will schedule the 1-hour bench next Thursday; Maya will share retention matrix.
[35:25] Priya: can we request a short artifact that lists all places PHI could appear in logs? that helps legal sign-off.
[35:32] Liam: yes we'll run a quick grep-based scan and produce a hit-list.
[35:36] Sofia: action items in the doc, i'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the bench.
[35:42] Graham: thanks — one last ask, can Redwood provide a sample audit export in NDJSON so our SIEM can ingest a sample?
[35:50] Liam: yes, i'll generate NDJSON sample and a schema file.
[35:55] Maya: thanks everyone.
[36:00] (meeting ends, small post-call 1:1 between Sofia and Priya offline)

Artifacts referenced:
- SOC2 Type II (redacted) — link to be shared by Sofia
- Nginx config snippets for proxy buffer settings (Liam)
- Audit log sample NDJSON + schema (Liam)
- Bench script + docker runner (Liam)
- Retention matrix from legal (Maya)

Notes about transcription noise: occasional dropped request_id shown as '-', minor speaker mislabels, and a few word swaps (KMS spelled K-M-S).
